ing: divided: 4 for lentils, plus rice water
st: Put the lentils, [[4 cups]] water, turmeric and [[1 tsp]] salt in a pot and bring to a boil. Skim off any foam.
Lower the heat, partly cover and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft and soupy.
Cook the rice with [[2.25 cups]] water and a pinch of salt: boil, then cover and cook on low for 15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Heat the ghee in a small pan over medium heat.
Add the cumin seeds and dried chilies and cook for 20 seconds until they sizzle.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until golden, then stir in the garlic, ginger and tomato for 3 minutes.
Pour the hot spice mix into the lentils and stir.
Simmer 5 minutes more, taste and add the remaining salt if needed.
Serve the dal over rice, with pickles or a simple vegetable on the side.
Mix the flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, then add warm water a little at a time and knead for 8 minutes into a smooth firm dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the chicken, onion, garlic, ginger, cilantro, cumin, soy sauce, oil, [[1 tsp]] salt and pepper in a bowl.
Divide the dough into 30 small balls and roll each into a thin round about 3 inches wide, with thinner edges.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of a wrapper.
Pleat the edge around the filling and twist to seal at the top, or fold it into a half moon.
Oil a steamer basket and boil water in the pot below.
Arrange the momos with space between them and steam over high heat for 12 to 15 minutes until the filling reaches 165°F (74°C).
Serve hot right away with momo achar for dipping.

ing: soaked in hot water 10 minutes, or to taste
st: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden, then remove.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the tomatoes and garlic for 8 minutes until the tomatoes soften and blister.
Drain the soaked chilies.
Put the tomatoes, garlic, chilies, sesame seeds, ginger and cumin in a blender.
Blend into a thick sauce, adding a splash of water if too thick.
Pour into a bowl and stir in the cilantro, lemon juice and salt.
Taste and adjust the salt and heat. Serve at room temperature with momos.
Cook the noodles in boiling water according to the package. Drain, rinse and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric and chili flakes and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken and stir for 3 minutes until it turns white.
Pour in the broth and add the carrots. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage and simmer for 5 minutes. The chicken must reach 165°F (74°C).
Season the soup with the salt and stir well.
Divide the noodles into bowls, ladle the hot soup over them, and top with cilantro.
Mix the rice flour, sugar, cardamom and salt in a bowl.
Stir in the melted butter and mashed banana.
Slowly add the milk, whisking, until you have a thick pourable batter like pancake batter that falls in ribbons.
Rest the batter for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide pot to 350°F (175°C).
Pour batter through a funnel or squeeze bottle in a circle, about 4 inches wide, directly into the hot oil, making a ring.
Fry for 2 minutes until golden underneath, then flip and fry for 2 minutes more.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve warm or at room temperature with tea or curry.

ing: fermented mustard greens, or use sauerkraut rinsed
st: Soak the dried gundruk in warm water for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water and chop it.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add the cumin seeds, then the onion and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and green chilies and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and turmeric and cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Stir in the gundruk and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the water and salt and simmer for 10 minutes.
Taste, adjust the salt and serve hot as a sour soup or as a side with rice.
Whisk the rice flour, water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into a smooth thin batter and rest for 15 minutes.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pan, cook half the onion with the garlic and ginger for 3 minutes.
Add the beef, cumin, chili flakes and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cook for 8 minutes, breaking up the meat, until it reaches 160°F (71°C). Stir in the tomato for 2 minutes.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat with a little oil.
Pour a ladle of batter and swirl to make a thin crepe about 7 inches wide.
Cook for 2 minutes until the base sets.
Spread the beef over the crepe and add some of the remaining onion. Crack an egg on top and spread it with a spoon.
Cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the egg is fully set.
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve hot, cut into wedges.

ing: split black lentils or yellow split peas
st: Drain the soaked lentils and grind them in a food processor with a few spoons of water into a thick, fluffy paste.
Mix in the garlic, ginger, cumin, asafoetida, chili, cilantro and salt.
Beat the paste with a spoon for 2 minutes to make it light.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in a patty of batter about 3 inches wide and flatten gently.
Cook for 3 minutes until golden and set, then flip.
Cook the second side for 3 minutes. If using eggs, crack one onto the patty after flipping, cover, and cook until set.
Drain on paper towels, adding more oil to the pan for each batch.
Serve warm with achar or chutney.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and add the cumin seeds for 20 seconds.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until golden.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric and chili powder and cook for 5 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the potatoes, bamboo shoots, black-eyed peas, salt and water.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Mash a few potato cubes against the pot to thicken the broth.
Taste, adjust the salt and sprinkle with cilantro. Serve with rice.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes. Cool a little and crush them lightly.
Mix the molasses, sesame, coconut, ghee and cardamom into a thick, sticky filling.
Mix the rice flour with the salt and slowly stir in hot water until it forms a dough.
Knead the warm dough for 5 minutes until smooth and soft. Cover with a damp cloth.
Pinch off pieces the size of a golf ball and shape each into a small cup.
Place about [[1 tsp]] of filling inside and pinch the top closed into a pointed fig shape. Seal very well so the filling does not leak.
Oil a steamer basket and bring water to a boil in the pot below.
Steam the yomari for 15 to 20 minutes until the dough looks shiny and slightly translucent.
Cool for 5 minutes and serve warm. The filling will be very hot.
